text: This course starts at the very beginning: the JavaScript you'll be writing inside ServiceNow scripts starting next chapter. First, the three ways to declare a variable, and the types of values they can hold.

Declare a variable with the keyword var, and it's function-scoped. Here, we declare a variable called message inside an if-block, assigning it the text Critical. Even after that if-block closes, the variable is still readable for the rest of the function. var leaks out of blocks like if, for, and while - it only respects the boundaries of the whole function.

Declare that same variable with let instead, and it's block-scoped - it only exists inside the nearest curly braces. Try to read it after the if-block closes, and you get a reference error, because it no longer exists. const works the same way for scoping, but adds one more rule: once you assign a value with const, you can never reassign it. Try to set maxRetries to a new number after declaring it with const, and JavaScript throws a type error.

Every value in JavaScript falls into one of these types. String for text, like a ticket number in quotes. Number for any numeric value - JavaScript doesn't separate integers from decimals the way some languages do. Boolean for true or false. Null and undefined both mean emptiness, but differently: undefined means a variable was declared and never assigned a value; null means a developer deliberately set it to nothing. And Object, which covers everything else, including the record-like structures you'll work with heavily once this course gets into ServiceNow's own APIs.

The typeof operator tells you what type a value actually is at runtime, which matters once you're checking data that came back from a ServiceNow API. It correctly reports string, number, boolean, and undefined. But there's a famous, decades-old quirk: typeof null returns the word object, not null. If you need to detect null specifically, don't rely on typeof - compare the value directly against null instead.
var leaks out of blocks, let and const don't, and typeof has one quirk worth memorizing. Next up: operators and control flow - how your scripts actually make decisions and repeat work.
